{{short description|American mathematician, statistician and professor}}
'''Richard Burton McHugh''' (October 25, 1923 – June 1, 2016) was an American statistician. McHugh was a professor of biometry at [[University of Minnesota School of Public Health]] for over 30 years.

== Early life and education ==
McHugh was born in [[Villard, Minnesota]]<ref name=lib-umn-edu/>  and grew up in Minneapolis, MN. 

He earned a bachelor of arts in statistics with a minor in mathematics, magna cum laude, in 1944 from [[University of Minnesota]]. He completed a master of arts in 1949.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://docplayer.net/65718739-University-of-minnesota.html|title=UNIVERSITY OF MINNESOTA - PDF|website=docplayer.net|access-date=2019-02-27}}</ref> McHugh earned a doctor of philosophy at University of Minnesota in 1954. His dissertation was titled ''On the scaling of psychological data by latent structure analysis''.<ref>{{Cite thesis|title=On the scaling of psychological data by latent structure analysis.|date=1954|language=English|first=Richard Burton|last=McHugh|oclc=11196868}}</ref> His advisors were [[Leonid Hurwicz]] and Jacob Bearman.<ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
Mchugh  was Assistant Professor of Statistics and Psychology at [[Iowa State University]] in [[Ames, Iowa]] from 1950 until 1954 when he was appointed Associate Professor.<ref name=lib-umn-edu>{{cite web |url=https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1566 |website=University of Minnesota Library Archives |title= Biographical Sketch | access-date=22 August 2022}}</ref>
In 1956 he began working at the University of Minnesota in Minneapolis as Associate Professor of Biostatistics in the School of Public Health; he became Professor of Biometry in 1961; and was appointed Professor and Director, Division of Biometry in 1968.
<ref name=lib-umn-edu/> He served on the faculty at [[University of Minnesota School of Public Health]] for over 30 years.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.startribune.com/obituaries/detail/138534/|title=Obituary for Richard B. McHugh|website=Star Tribune|access-date=2019-02-27}}</ref> 

He was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 1967.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.amstat.org/ASA/Your-Career/Awards/ASA-Fellows-list.aspx|title=ASA Fellows list|accessdate=2019-02-27}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
A practicing [[Roman Catholic]], Richard McHugh was married to Rosemary McHugh, nee Jarvis, with whom he had 2 daughters and 3 sons. He was preceded in death by his wife, daughter and 10 siblings.<ref name=":1" />
